## 0b8631a5fc70

**Reproduced teaching shortcut — last-marker rule survives the demonstrations.** Generator SHA-256 `ad2a881eb69521352ff4960eec3d61716e1c265618d6c0961e1b74ccd036dad7`; canonical rule hash `c328d1c4e7f4`. For seed `0`, consecutive samples `8,9,10` each contain exactly one `8` and one `9`. Therefore the wrong rule “use the last row-major 8 and last row-major 9 as the vector, then erase all markers” exactly matches the intended first-marker rule on all three demonstrations. Sample `11` is a valid generated `extra_markers` query with two `8`s and two `9`s; it passes `self_check`, but the rival output differs from the authoritative Racket output.

Evidence: compact metadata in `checks/audit/0b8631a5fc70/shortcut_witness.json`, the complete four-pair lesson in `checks/audit/0b8631a5fc70/lesson.json`, query input in `input.json`, rival output in `rival.json`, and supported canonical execution in `racket.json`. This is a lesson-assembly defect, not a label error. A deterministic schedule ensuring at least one multi-marker demonstration would refute it; no source was changed because this was audit-only.

## 0b8631a5fc70

**Conclusion: Reproduced teaching shortcut — first-marker versus last-marker ambiguity.** Audited generator SHA-256: `ad2a881eb69521352ff4960eec3d61716e1c265618d6c0961e1b74ccd036dad7`; canonical rule hash `c328d1c4e7f4`. No source was modified.

The current generator’s documented rule uses the first row-major color-8 and first row-major color-9 markers to define a translation vector. A current-source episode generated with seed `0`, start sample index `8`, three demonstrations and one query reproduces a plausible rival: use the last row-major 8 and last row-major 9 instead. Demonstrations at sample indices 8, 9, and 10 each contain exactly one 8 and one 9, so first-marker and last-marker rules produce identical labels. The query at sample index 11 contains two of each marker; the rival then predicts a different output.

The supported `arcpuzzles apply` command executed the canonical Racket rule on that query, confirmed catalog-rule hash agreement, and recorded generator-domain status `valid` with no validator errors. Its output SHA-256 is `869e5a7e07cba437623f081bde7231dc2195f6998cd811c9118579ad9f6eecff`; the rival output SHA-256 is `ca4d4896d6ab1e70f4b07913ce77f0b27d9174d1b78e4466bddc6aa5b9d5deea`.

The complete reproduction is `checks/audit/0b8631a5fc70-witness/shortcut_witness.json`, with the generated lesson, query input, rival output, build script, and Racket receipt beside it. The combined audit also found no task-local/frozen tests and no semantic contract (`checks/audit/0b8631a5fc70-combined/checks/0b8631a5fc70_audit_summary.json`). A future repair should guarantee that every three-demo lesson containing an `extra_markers` query also exposes an extra-marker demonstration, or declare and execute this rival in lesson identifiability checks.
